precepts.text: And king Solomon made a navy of ships in Ezion-geber, which is beside Eloth, on the shore of the Red sea. Hiram sent shipmen that had knowledge of the sea: the maritime men. And they came to Ophir, and fetched from thence gold, four hundred and twenty talents. Ezion-geber sits at the northern tip of the Red Sea's Gulf of Aqaba, near the region where the tribes entered the Euphrates. We had maritime trade going in Solomon's time, so it was no mystery for us to make it from Persia over to the Americas: the ports were there. Ivan Van Sertima's They Came Before Columbus speaks of Solomon's ships.
precepts.point: For through that country there was a great way to go, namely, of a year and a half: and the same region is called Arsareth. A year and a half of travel means stops along the way: the maritime ports. From the book Maritime Trade and the Movement of Culture, by the sister the teacher interviewed on the Quest voyage and whose museum in Charleston the nation plans to visit: the Red Sea and Indian Ocean connected Africa to the wider world as early as the third century BCE, trading gold, ivory, spices, and textiles with Arabia, India, Persia, and China, with cultural diffusion along the coasts.

note.label: 250 Years of Celebration; 400 Years of Sweat Equity!

precepts.why:
“For through that country there was a great way to go, namely, of a year and a half”. If it took us a year and a half to get from one area to another, don’t you think we were making stops? Maritime means things connected with the sea, oceans and navigation: shipping, commerce, naval operations. We were running those ports, and even where it was not us particularly, we had understanding with the nations we passed by. The Red Sea and the Indian Ocean connected Africa to the wider world as early as the third century BCE, with trade to Arabia, India, Persia and China.

Solomon had a navy of ships: “And king Solomon made a navy of ships in Ezion–geber, which is beside Eloth, on the shore of the Red sea, in the land of Edom. And Hiram sent in the navy his servants, shipmen that had knowledge of the sea, with the servants of Solomon.” Shipmen that had knowledge of the sea: those are the maritime men.

Ezion-geber is at the northern tip of the Red Sea’s Gulf of Aqaba, by modern-day Aqaba in Jordan and Eilat. That is very near the region where the brothers entered into the Euphrates. “And they came to Ophir, and fetched from thence gold, four hundred and twenty talents, and brought it to king Solomon.” Ophir is not far from those same areas.

So we had maritime trade going on even in Solomon’s time. It was no mystery for us to make it from where we were, out of Persia, over to the Americas, because those ports were there. That is how the journey took a year and a half, stopping at the ports, until we came into the region called Arsareth, the land Columbus identified with America.

precepts.text: Upon the Jebusites and the other nations left in the land did Solomon levy a tribute of bondservice unto this day: they were our servants.
precepts.point: He that remaineth shall be for our God, a governor in Judah, and Ekron as a Jebusite: as David smote the Jebusites and Solomon levied a tribute of bondservice on those left in the land, they will be our servants. No oppressor shall pass through them any more, for now have I seen with mine eyes, as God looked upon the children of Israel and had respect unto them.

note.label: Zionism in the Face of Syria & Hezbollah

precepts.why:
“And all the people that were left of the Amorites, Hittites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites, which were not of the children of Israel, Their children that were left after them in the land, whom the children of Israel also were not able utterly to destroy, upon those did Solomon levy a tribute of bondservice unto this day.”

They were our servants, our slaves. The Jebusites left in the land did not rule over Israel; Solomon put them under a tribute of bondservice.

So when we go back to the last part of Zechariah 9:7, “and Ekron as a Jebusite”, it means they are going to be our servants. Those that are left of the Philistines will be to Israel what the Jebusites were to David and Solomon, while he that remaineth of Israel “shall be as a governor in Judah.” The pride of the Philistines is cut off, and the order is turned back the way God set it.

precepts.text: Upon the people left of those nations did Solomon levy a tribute of bondservice unto this day.
precepts.point: The people that were left of the Amorites, Hittites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites, whom Israel was not able utterly to destroy, upon those did Solomon levy a tribute of bondservice unto this day. They were forced to become our bondservants.

note.label: Joshua 15: The Lot of the Tribe of Judah

precepts.why:
“And all the people that were left of the Amorites, Hittites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites, which were not of the children of Israel, Their children that were left after them in the land, whom the children of Israel also were not able utterly to destroy, upon those did Solomon levy a tribute of bondservice unto this day.”

The Jebusites that Judah could not drive out did not stay free among us. The people left of those nations, whom Israel was not able utterly to destroy, were forced to become our bondservants under Solomon; that is where “unto this day” ends up for them.

precepts.text: Of the children of Israel did Solomon make no bondmen, but they were men of war, his servants, his princes, his captains, and rulers of his chariots and his horsemen; five hundred and fifty chief officers bare rule over the people that wrought in the work.
precepts.point: The manner of the king came to pass under Solomon: he levied a tax, and the tax was men. Just as men go off to war, he sent them a month on and two months off to Lebanon, to prepare the timber and stones to build the house of the Lord.

note.label: 1 Samuel 8: Give Us a King Like All the Nations

precepts.why:
“But of the children of Israel did Solomon make no bondmen: but they were men of war, and his servants, and his princes, and his captains, and rulers of his chariots, and his horsemen.”

That is word for word the manner of the king Samuel described: “He will take your sons, and appoint them for himself, for his chariots, and to be his horsemen”, “And he will appoint him captains over thousands, and captains over fifties.”

“These were the chief of the officers that were over Solomon’s work, five hundred and fifty, which bare rule over the people that wrought in the work.” The king's work, the king's captains, the king's chariots: “and ye shall be his servants.”

precepts.text: Solomon by his own word is black, so the builder of the first temple was a black man.
precepts.point: The so-called Jews boast of the temple and their heritage in a land that does not belong to them, but the man who built the first temple was a black man, and the scripture says so plainly.

note.label: 1 Kings 9: The Most High Appears to Solomon a Second Time

precepts.why:
“I am black, but comely, O ye daughters of Jerusalem, as the tents of Kedar, as the curtains of Solomon.” Solomon by his own word is black.

So when Solomon “had finished the building of the house of the Lord”, and the Most High appeared to him the second time as at Gibeon, the man who built the first temple was a black man, and the scripture says so plainly. The so-called Jews boast of the temple and their heritage in a land that does not belong to them, but the builder of that temple was black.

precepts.text: If Israel will not hearken to do all his commandments, all these curses shall come and overtake them.
precepts.point: The house that was high and mighty would astonish everyone who passed by, and they would ask why the Most High had done this, and the answer is because Israel forsook the Most High who brought their fathers out of Egypt and took hold of other gods. This shows the Most High is not all love, for it says therefore he brought upon them all this evil.

note.label: 1 Kings 9: The Most High Appears to Solomon a Second Time

precepts.why:
“But it shall come to pass, if thou wilt not hearken unto the voice of the Lord thy God, to observe to do all his commandments and his statutes which I command thee this day; that all these curses shall come upon thee, and overtake thee”.

This is the same warning Moses gave in the law, and the Most High gives it again to Solomon: “if ye shall at all turn from following me, ye or your children, and will not keep my commandments and my statutes”, “Then will I cut off Israel out of the land which I have given them”. Disobedience brings the curse of scattering, and it reaches not only that generation but the seed after them.

The Most High is not all love. When they ask why this came, the answer is, “Because they forsook the Lord their God”, “therefore hath the Lord brought upon them all this evil.”

precepts.text: Israel shall become an astonishment, a proverb, and a byword among all nations where the Most High shall lead them.
precepts.point: The house that was high and mighty would astonish everyone who passed by, and they would ask why the Most High had done this, and the answer is because Israel forsook the Most High who brought their fathers out of Egypt and took hold of other gods. This shows the Most High is not all love, for it says therefore he brought upon them all this evil.

note.label: 1 Kings 9: The Most High Appears to Solomon a Second Time

precepts.why:
“And thou shalt become an astonishment, a proverb, and a byword, among all nations whither the Lord shall lead thee.”

The Most High told Solomon the same: “Israel shall be a proverb and a byword among all people: And at this house, which is high, every one that passeth by it shall be astonished, and shall hiss”. The house that was high and mighty would astonish everyone who passed by.

They would ask, “Why hath the Lord done thus unto this land, and to this house?” and the answer: Israel forsook the Most High who brought their fathers out of the land of Egypt, and took hold of other gods. The curse of the law and the word to Solomon are one.

precepts.text: Bondmen and bondmaids are to be taken of the heathen round about, so the tribute of bondservice was lawful.
precepts.point: Of the children of Israel Solomon made no bondmen, but they were men of war, his servants, princes, captains, and rulers of his chariots and horsemen; instead of enslaving his own people he built them up and gave them positions.

note.label: 1 Kings 9: The Most High Appears to Solomon a Second Time

precepts.why:
“Both thy bondmen, and thy bondmaids, which thou shalt have, shall be of the heathen that are round about you; of them shall ye buy bondmen and bondmaids.” Bondmen and bondmaids are to be taken of the heathen round about.

So when Solomon levied a tribute of bondservice on “all the people that were left of the Amorites, Hittites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites, which were not of the children of Israel”, it was lawful by the law.

“But of the children of Israel did Solomon make no bondmen: but they were men of war, and his servants, and his princes, and his captains, and rulers of his chariots, and his horsemen.” Instead of enslaving his own people, he built them up and gave them positions.

precepts.text: The Most High left the nations to prove Israel whether they would keep his way as their fathers did.
precepts.point: Of the children of Israel Solomon made no bondmen, but they were men of war, his servants, princes, captains, and rulers of his chariots and horsemen; instead of enslaving his own people he built them up and gave them positions.

note.label: 1 Kings 9: The Most High Appears to Solomon a Second Time

precepts.why:
“And the anger of the Lord was hot against Israel; and he said, Because that this people hath transgressed my covenant which I commanded their fathers, and have not hearkened unto my voice; I also will not henceforth drive out any from before them of the nations which Joshua left when he died: That through them I may prove Israel, whether they will keep the way of the Lord to walk therein, as their fathers did keep it, or not.”

That is why there were still Amorites, Hittites, Perizzites, Hivites and Jebusites in the land in Solomon’s day, “whom the children of Israel also were not able utterly to destroy”. The Most High left the nations to prove Israel whether they would keep his way as their fathers did.

precepts.text: These are the nations the Most High left to prove Israel and to teach them war.
precepts.point: Of the children of Israel Solomon made no bondmen, but they were men of war, his servants, princes, captains, and rulers of his chariots and horsemen; instead of enslaving his own people he built them up and gave them positions.

note.label: 1 Kings 9: The Most High Appears to Solomon a Second Time

precepts.why:
“Now these are the nations which the Lord left, to prove Israel by them, even as many of Israel as had not known all the wars of Canaan”. These are the nations the Most High left to prove Israel and to teach them war.

Those same nations, their children “that were left after them in the land”, are the ones Solomon put under a tribute of bondservice, while the children of Israel served as his men of war, his captains and the rulers of his chariots and horsemen.

precepts.text: If Israel turns from the commandments, the Most High will cast the house out of his sight and make Israel a proverb and a byword among all people.
precepts.point: The same warning was spoken over Solomon: turning from the commandments would make Israel a proverb and a byword, an astonishment to all who passed by. That is exactly how the nations look at scattered Israel today.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 29: Hezekiah Cleanses the House of the Lord

precepts.why:
The same warning was spoken over Solomon: “if ye shall at all turn from following me, ye or your children, and will not keep my commandments and my statutes”, “Then will I cut off Israel out of the land which I have given them; and this house, which I have hallowed for my name, will I cast out of my sight; and Israel shall be a proverb and a byword among all people”.

At this house “every one that passeth by it shall be astonished, and shall hiss”, and they will ask why. The answer: “Because they forsook the Lord their God, who brought forth their fathers out of the land of Egypt, and have taken hold upon other gods”.

Hezekiah saw it come to pass: “the wrath of the Lord was upon Judah and Jerusalem, and he hath delivered them to trouble, to astonishment, and to hissing, as ye see with your eyes.” And, “our fathers have fallen by the sword, and our sons and our daughters and our wives are in captivity for this.” That is exactly how the nations look at scattered Israel today: a proverb and a byword, an astonishment to all who pass by.
